takeaways: Plastic flow begins at yield; cold working raises flow stress with strain, while hot working keeps it low by recrystallisation.
Rolling reduces thickness by pulling strip through rolls; defects come from uneven flow, friction and roll bending.
Forging shapes metal by repeated squeezing; flash and gutter control die filling, and grain flow follows the contour.
Extrusion pushes a billet through a die; direct extrusion has container friction, indirect extrusion reduces it, and impact extrusion makes cups.
Wire drawing pulls rather than pushes; the drawing stress must stay below the metal's yield strength or the wire breaks.
Every bulk forming load is approximately mean flow stress times contact area, corrected for friction and shape.
Powder metallurgy compacts and sinters powder; powder flow, apparent density, green density and sintering control final quality.
Defect choice and process choice depend on temperature, friction, die geometry and stress state.
